clue.text: Separate clue for trifle?

parts.note: the six letters of trifle in a different order
out, as in out of order, is a standard instruction to rearrange the letters before it

explanation.surface: Someone asking for a crossword clue for the pudding trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer is not built from 'trifle', it is the instruction that would clue it, with OUT naming what was done to FILTER's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To filter out is to separate unwanted matter from the rest.

clue.text: Top quality match enveloped by lots of passion

indicators.note: the match is wrapped inside the other letters

parts.note: FIRE, a word for passion, without its last letter
a vesta is an old word for a short match

explanation.surface: A thrilling contest full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting contest, but it is the kind you strike: a vesta is a short wax match, a word now met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-star, as in hotel ratings, means of the highest quality.

clue.text: From time to time, look to fate

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter

parts.note: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of LOOKTO

explanation.surface: Advice to trust in destiny every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' does double duty in the surface but the fodder runs across the gap: L-O-o-K-T-o.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fate in life.

clue.text: Unusual case passed on to up the intensity

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters of case are rearranged

parts.note: passed on is a euphemism for died, and the late means the dead

explanation.surface: A strange court case was handed on so as to make things more serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges CASE as ESCA, followed by LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to increase or intensify, as a conflict escalates.

clue.text: Go round the bend endlessly in French department

indicators.note: endlessly means without either end, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: to corner is to go round a bend, as a car does

explanation.surface: Losing your mind for ever somewhere in a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round the bend' looks like the idiom for going mad, but it is CORNER; 'endlessly' trims both ends. The Orne is a department of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Orne is one of the numbered administrative departments of France, in Normandy.

clue.text: Desk, left out with salt during religious teaching in church

parts.note: TABLE without its L

indicators.note: the salt goes inside the religious teaching

parts.note: RE, religious education, the school subject
NaCl, the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: A pew-side lectern and a salt cellar at a scripture lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' usually tempts a solver towards a sailor (AB or TAR); here it is chemistry. RE, religious education, is the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a place of worship, especially a nonconformist or Mormon church.

clue.text: Running about on leave in part of the Western US

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
re = on, concerning
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Jogging around while on holiday out West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On leave' reads as holiday, but the two words split apart and each gives its own chunk, which is why the same little word appears twice in different roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state on the Pacific coast of the United States.

clue.text: Some cards for football team

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
the short name of Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club

explanation.surface: Yellow and red cards being shown to a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Football sets up booking cards; the cards are a suit, and Hearts is a Scottish club.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is both a card suit and the usual name of Heart of Midlothian FC.

clue.text: Exposed appliance for removing water from locks in Scottish town

indicators.note: exposed means with the cover taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.words: appliance for removing water from locks
parts.note: a hairdrier dries wet hair, the locks

explanation.surface: An exposed hairdryer in a Scottish town, as if a news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' strips the H and R from HAIRDRIER; 'locks' is hair, not door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Airdrie is a town in North Lanarkshire, east of Glasgow.

clue.text: Polish ruse to muddle Trump, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters are to be muddled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A cunning trick from Poland designed to confuse the US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' leads with its capital to Poland; it is only letters. The definition is a jibe at Donald Trump's perceived fondness for Russia, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russophile admires Russia, which critics have said of Trump.

clue.text: One entering vacant, dilapidated palace

indicators.note: the I goes into the other word
falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as it stands, then rearranged with the I
I = one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A squatter moving into an empty, run-down palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The run-down empty palace turns out to be the grandest one of all: the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Pope's official residence in Rome is a palace, and the most famous one there is.

clue.text: Current supplier from Spain quit over stealing stereo, essentially

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so the letters go inside
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to quit a job is to resign

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the two middle letters of stereo

parts.note: the two central letters of stereo

explanation.surface: A Spanish power company boss resigns over the theft of a hi-fi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a time word, but it is electric current; 'over' signals reading backwards, not 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: An energiser gives energy; a battery brand uses the name for its cells, which supply electric current.

clue.text: Humble Earl limps around

indicators.note: the letters are moved around

parts.note: E = earl, a standard abbreviation
anagram fodder with the E

explanation.surface: A modest aristocrat hobbling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble Earl' reads as one phrase, but 'Humble' is the definition and the earl is just E.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and humble both describe a modest, unpretentious life.

clue.text: Case of archetypal sucker stopping to pay for "financial security"

indicators.note: plugging a gap in the other word

parts.note: to meet a cost is to pay for it

indicators.note: the casing, the outer letters, of the word

parts.note: the outer letters of ArchetypaL
a tick is a bloodsucking parasite

explanation.surface: A typical gullible customer holding up payment for a pension scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a dupe, but it is a bloodsucker: the TICK. AL and TICK together fill MEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal ticket is a person or thing relied on as a source of income.

clue.text: Somehow stop dismal singer

indicators.note: arranged in some way or other

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A plea to silence a dreary vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'dismal singer' as a phrase, but 'dismal' belongs with 'stop' as the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrower term: someone who sings or composes psalms, so a particular kind of singer.

clue.text: Chicken specialist collects old flightless birds

parts.note: Nando's, the chain of chicken restaurants
O = old, a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A poultry restaurant gathering up aged ostriches.
explanation.walkthrough: Nando's is a peri-peri chicken restaurant chain, common in Britain. Nandoo (or nandu) is another name for the rhea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nandoos, or rheas, are large flightless South American birds.

clue.text: Russian card game that doesn't use clubs is back — back in Russia

indicators.note: that doesn't use means the letter for clubs is left out

parts.note: canasta is a rummy-style card game
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way round
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian card game played without clubs is returning to Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that doesn't use clubs' turns CANASTA into ANASTA, 'is back' gives SI and 'back in Russia' gives A. Anastasia was the daughter of the last Tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia is a Russian name, borne by the Grand Duchess, so a Russian woman.

clue.text: Regularly shoot and record stuff as 3-D image

indicators.note: at regular intervals, every second letter

parts.note: the 2nd and 4th letters of sHoOt
to log is to record
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Filming and saving footage as a three-dimensional picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot and record' paints filming; only HO comes from 'shoot', and 'record' and 'stuff' are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hologram is a three-dimensional image made with lasers.

clue.text: Most of country upset over one's failure to develop

indicators.note: most of a word is nearly all of it, so the country loses just its final letter
turned upside down, which in a down clue reverses it

parts.note: SENEGAL without its L
one's = one is, I'S

explanation.surface: Much of a nation unhappy at someone's stunted growth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first part on top of the second. The country is Senegal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agenesis is the failure of an organ or body part to develop.

clue.text: Hanging around work, walking with a bounce

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so the word for hanging surrounds the word for work

parts.note: lolling = hanging loosely, like a tongue
OP = opus, a work

explanation.surface: Loafing about at the office, then bouncing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging around work' reads as idling, but 'around' is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move with a clumsy bounding gait.

clue.text: Something pointed close to some farm animals

indicators.note: the close, last letter, of the word

parts.note: the last letter of somE
a PIG and a RAM

explanation.surface: A sharp object lying near livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' suggests something sharp to touch; the point is in the wit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist on a stock phrase: epigrams are proverbially pointed, their point being a sharp witty sting rather than a physical tip.

clue.text: Whole of Ireland absorbing part of the Bible

indicators.note: taking the letters into itself

parts.note: Éire, the Irish name for Ireland
NT = New Testament

explanation.surface: All of Ireland soaking up scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whole of Ireland' reads as one phrase; 'Whole' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the entire cake and the whole cake are the same cake, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Prayers in bed?

definitions.meaning: the Catholic sequence of prayers counted on beads
a flower bed, specifically one planted with roses

explanation.surface: Saying one's prayers before sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests bedtime, but it is a flower bed; the question mark flags the second, rarer sense of rosary.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a sequence of prayers, and also a bed of roses.

clue.text: Lead piping over new houses

indicators.note: the words house the answer inside them

parts.note: pipinG OVER New

explanation.surface: Old lead water pipes installed in new homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead piping' is the plumbing picture; 'Lead' is the verb to rule and the pipes are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a party that governs a country leads it.

clue.text: Attempts to shoot fish for select party

parts.note: a take is one filmed attempt at a scene
an ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A film crew's attempts to film fish for an exclusive gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' could mean fire at the fish; it is filming, and 'select party' is a verb and object, not an exclusive do.
explanation.definitionFit: To take sides is to choose which party to support.

clue.text: South American iron is reliable

parts.note: SA = South America(n)
Fe, the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A tribute to the dependability of Latin American steelwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Two abbreviations: the continent and the element.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a safe bet or a safe driver is one you can rely on.

clue.text: By the way, a very big rugby player is boring

indicators.note: the player bores into the other letters

parts.note: as written
OS = outsize, a clothing size
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: An aside that a huge rugby forward is dull company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it is the drilling kind: PROP bores into A…OS. 'Very big rugby player' wants to be one person; OS and PROP are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used to change the subject, means by the way.

clue.text: Discharge Manx cat?

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about something oozing from a tailless cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats, from the Isle of Man, are born without tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Pus is the thick fluid discharged from an infected wound.

clue.text: Goes to bed in garret I reserved

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

parts.note: garRET I REServed

explanation.surface: Someone turning in for the night in an attic room they had booked.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across all three words, straddling the lone I.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal, slightly old-fashioned sense: one retires for the night, withdrawing to one's bedroom.

clue.text: Scratching head, remaining prophet provides bottles of drink?

parts.note: OTHER (remaining, as in the other ones) without its O
Moses, the Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A puzzled prophet handing out flasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' pictures puzzlement; it is an instruction to drop a first letter. The question mark is because thermoses hold drink rather than being bottles of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermoses are vacuum flasks for keeping drinks hot or cold.
